title: Operate monitoring, detection, and alert triage
question: When should a signal be escalated, suppressed, or used to tune detection?
scenario: UEBA flags an administrator who authenticates from two regions within ten minutes. A VPN gateway shows a corporate egress address, and a change ticket shows an approved maintenance window.
focalRelation: signal --severity plus confidence plus asset/identity context--> triage corroborated consequential activity --authorized response--> escalation benign explanation with evidence --narrow time/host/source scope and expiry--> suppression unknown evidence --remains open or escalates by consequence--> investigation known outcome --updates threshold with missed-event review--> detection tuning

nodes.label: UEBA signal
nodes.detail: Two-region administrator anomaly; a model score is a prioritization input, not the disposition.

nodes.label: VPN session
nodes.detail: Corporate egress session tying network path, user, and source time to the activity.

nodes.label: Managed device and MFA
nodes.detail: Subject and device assurance evidence for the observed session.

nodes.label: Maintenance ticket
nodes.detail: Approved target, task, time, owner, and expiry against which activity is compared.

nodes.label: Target command history
nodes.detail: Observed operations that confirm approved work or expose deviation and impact.

nodes.label: Triage outcome
nodes.detail: Escalation or documented benign closure plus scoped, expiring tuning and false-negative review.

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: UEBA flags an administrator who authenticates from two regions within ten minutes. A VPN gateway shows a corporate egress address, and a change ticket shows an approved maintenance window.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: Severity and confidence are different dimensions; a low-confidence signal on a critical asset may still deserve review.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: A high alert count proves monitoring is effective. Volume can reflect noisy rules, duplicate sources, or poor triage; effectiveness requires meaningful coverage, timely decisions, and known outcomes.

statuses.n6: score alone cannot close or escalate

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: Do not close solely on the anomaly or escalate solely on the model score. Correlate VPN session identity, device, ticket, MFA, target systems, and command history. If the evidence matches the approved work, document the benign cause and tune the model or exception with an expiry; if it does not, escalate and protect the account under incident procedures.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a detection signal, classify and prioritize it, select corroborating evidence, escalate or close it, and improve the use case without hiding meaningful risk. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

statuses.n6: scoped expiry/tuning or incident escalation recorded

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Scope the exception to the approved host, window, and source; retain counts and an expiry; add a separate alert for deviation from the maintenance pattern. A broad suppression can hide credential abuse and removes the evidence needed to reassess the rule.

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

statuses.n6: host/window/source exception expires; deviation alert retained

prediction.prompt: When should a signal be escalated, suppressed, or used to tune detection?

options.label: A high alert count proves monitoring is effective.
options.feedback: Incorrect: Volume can reflect noisy rules, duplicate sources, or poor triage; effectiveness requires meaningful coverage, timely decisions, and known outcomes.

options.label: Escalate the two-region login as confirmed compromise without checking the VPN or change window.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the alert is a triage lead. Correlate the corporate egress path, approved maintenance, actor, device, actions, and corroborating signals before disposition.

options.label: Do not close solely on the anomaly or escalate solely on the model score
options.feedback: Correct for this scenario: this answer uses the displayed relation and preserves its scope. Volume can reflect noisy rules, duplicate sources, or poor triage; effectiveness requires meaningful coverage, timely decisions, and known outcomes.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

transfer.prompt: An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise.

options.label: Scope the exception to the approved host, window, and source
options.feedback: Correct. Scope the exception to the approved host, window, and source; retain counts and an expiry; add a separate alert for deviation from the maintenance pattern. A broad suppression can hide credential abuse and removes the evidence needed to reassess the rule.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Do not close solely on the anomaly or escalate solely on the model score. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Scope the exception to the approved host, window, and source; retain counts and an expiry; add a separate alert for deviation from the maintenance pattern. A broad suppression can hide credential abuse and removes the evidence needed to reassess the rule.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: Do not close solely on the anomaly or escalate solely on the model score. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A behavior model assigns a high anomaly score to a service account, but asset role, maintenance window, and command details are missing. What should triage do?

options.label: Automatically isolate every asset with a high model score
options.feedback: A score without context can create unsafe false positives; automation needs bounded confidence and rollback conditions.

options.label: Add asset, identity, change, and command context before deciding the alert
options.feedback: Correct. Context turns an anomaly into a reviewable detection decision.

options.label: Suppress the alert because service accounts normally behave differently from users
options.feedback: Service identities can be compromised; distinct behavior calls for tuned context, not blanket suppression.

retry.hint: A score ranks attention; it does not supply the absent business and event context.

takeaway: Do not close solely on the anomaly or escalate solely on the model score.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: Implemented in 5 stable decision states: UEBA signal creates triage obligation Triage outcome; VPN session adds network and time evidence Triage outcome. The model keeps UEBA signal, VPN session, Managed device and MFA, Maintenance ticket, Target command history, Triage outcome distinct. Its changed case is “An analyst proposes suppressing all failed-login alerts from a service account because overnight maintenance creates noise.” and every option returns to a named repair state.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Severity and confidence are separate dimensions, so even a low-confidence signal on a critical asset may require review. Close, escalate, or tune only after corroboration, and bound any exception by source, host, time, owner, and expiry.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A branched decision view can compare confidence, severity, corroboration, escalation, closure, and bounded tuning; the initial signal/outcome pair does not.
